listenings.text: Hi everyone, it's Daniel Price, your moderator for Friday's panel. Just a few notes before we start. The panel is at eleven, in the Main Hall, and it lasts forty-five minutes. Each panelist has two minutes for an opening statement, so please keep it short. After that, I will ask questions, and I want a real discussion, not four separate speeches. If you disagree with another panelist, say so, but stay polite. And please don't read from your phone. The last fifteen minutes are for questions from the audience. See you on Friday.

Many smart people say almost nothing on a panel. They wait for the perfect moment, and the moment never comes. Here is a simple method. First, acknowledge the other speaker: say what is true in their point. Second, add your view. A sentence with although or even though does both jobs at the same time. For example: although the courts are slow, the outcomes are good. Third, support your view with one fact or one example. Don't try to win the argument. The audience remembers the panelist who made the discussion better, even though she didn't speak the most.

extra_audio.text: Daniel Price sent the panelists a message about the format. On Friday morning, Eduarda prepared her two-minute opening statement. At eleven, the moderator introduced the four panelists. Mark Ellison said that Brazil was too risky for investors. Eduarda agreed with part of his point, but she gave a counterargument with real numbers. In the last fifteen minutes, the audience asked her three questions.
